requiredFindings.title: Define traversal that actually discovers pnpm sibling dependencies
requiredFindings.detail: LD-C2B0-1 seeds the unit root's ancestor node_modules directories, and LD-C2B0-3 adds each package's own child node_modules. Neither rule reaches the siblings claimed by LD-C2B0-4. After node_modules/foo resolves to node_modules/.pnpm/foo@1/node_modules/foo, the target's own nested directory is .../foo/node_modules; foo's dependency bar is instead a sibling at node_modules/.pnpm/foo@1/node_modules/bar. That directory is not below foo, and .pnpm was deliberately excluded from the initial listing. Enumerating the target as a row does not itself enumerate the target's parent. A layout following the explicit traversal can therefore omit an ordinary pnpm dependency while the stated positive control expects it.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Specify the dependency-search directories queued for each resolved package target, including the enclosing virtual-store node_modules directory and relevant in-project ancestor search directories, with deterministic exclusions and no wholesale .pnpm-store scan. Preserve distinct installPath/realPath rows. Add a pnpm fixture with a sibling dependency reachable only through that virtual-store parent, plus scoped siblings and workspace-target ancestor lookup, and assert the exact visited-directory set as well as output rows.

requiredFindings.title: Define visited and row-merging rules for the package-link graph
requiredFindings.detail: Every link adds its target as a row and those target rows are enumerated in turn, but the plan gives no visited/queued identity or merge rule. Two aliases can point to the same real directory, a target can already have been encountered through another search directory, and valid package dependencies can form cycles through distinct symlinks to real directories. The one-link-level refusal does not stop such package-graph cycles. Treating a repeated installPath as impossible and refusing Order at line 89 would reject legitimate shared targets; simply re-enumerating them can loop or consume the ledger repeatedly. The 100,000-row bound only bounds distinct output rows, not revisits.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Specify charged worklist/visited state keyed by normalized project-relative directory/search-directory identity and a map keyed by installPath. Reuse equivalent rows and manifest captures, refuse inconsistent observations, and enumerate each required real directory/search location once while preserving alias rows. Distinguish a forbidden filesystem symlink chain from an allowed dependency cycle. Add shared-target aliases, repeated target discovery, a diamond dependency graph and an A-to-B-to-A package cycle; require deterministic complete rows and finite bounded work without an Order or Budget refusal caused solely by revisiting the graph.

requiredFindings.title: Separate non-dependency exclusions from read-set eligibility
requiredFindings.detail: The plan uses C1c-0's read_set_path to apply exclusions to packages and link targets, while also promising a first-party workspace target such as packages/x. In the declared C1c r2 interface, read_set_path returns Forbidden for an authorized path outside every node_modules tree. It cannot simultaneously serve as an unconditional workspace-target exclusion predicate and admit packages/x. The specified C1c pruned-tree opener also targets regular-file capture; an explicit directory-reach/exclusion interface is needed for layout traversal. Merely skipping the predicate for workspace targets would lose the promised VCS/Cargo/extent checks.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Define the C1c-0 interfaces the layout needs: safe no-follow directory reach and a non-dependency exclusion check that can classify first-party targets separately from dependency-tree read-set eligibility. First-party workspace targets must retain the ordinary opener/custody and Walk-origin reuse rules, while all targets preserve boundaries, ignorePaths, VCS, Cargo-output and exact custody-anchor exclusions. Reconcile this with the separately reviewed C1c interface before integration. Add an allowed packages/x target and forbidden workspace targets under Cargo output, VCS/custody anchors, ignorePaths and admitted boundaries, with no-open/no-read assertions for excluded targets.

requiredFindings.title: Own a freshness interval when no unfrozen batch can accept C2b-0
requiredFindings.detail: LD-C2B0-7 assigns the snapshot recipe change to C2b-0 but only says it joins whichever batch is open. It does not limit joining to before the final-input freeze or schedule an interval if no batch is open. The dependency chain permits C1c-0 to have refreshed separately before C2b-0 integrates, so the companion receipt then becomes stale anew. An existing batch may also already be frozen. Neither an earlier refresh nor adding edits after a pre-run review covers this later recipe. The plan's dependency on C1c r2 is explicitly subject to revision; the missing interval cases cannot be left implicit in that reference.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: State that C2b-0 may join an existing reviewed interval only before its final-input freeze. Otherwise it opens and owns a new interval with a fresh accepted baseline, exact receipt-specific deltas, pre-run review, frozen-input mechanical blind refresh and post-run review before dependent reliance. Track cumulative changes if an interval is already stale; an empty additional discovery delta does not make a previously stale discovery receipt current. Preserve passing output checks separately from freshness and update the C1c cross-reference to the agreed interval rules.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Describe the selected JSON profile rather than generic strict JSON
nonBlockingObservations.detail: identity::canonical::parse is narrower than ordinary strict JSON: it rejects floating-point numbers, negative zero, out-of-range integers, duplicate keys and depth beyond 32, including in unrelated manifest fields. For example, a manifest with valid string name/version and an unrelated numeric value 1.5 is valid JSON but refuses this reader. MAX_BYTES is only one of its constraints.
nonBlockingObservations.suggestedChange: Explicitly name this supported manifest profile and its typed refusal, and add representative profile-boundary cases. If ordinary JSON manifests with such unrelated values must be supported, select a bounded projection/parser that handles them while preserving exact captured bytes. Do not label all such refusals malformed JSON.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Distinguish the row-count check from complete record admission
nonBlockingObservations.detail: The statement that 100,000 rows admit cannot be a whole-record control through the existing identity canonical encoder: it has a 4 MiB limit, and 100,000 rows with the mandatory 64-character digest and five named fields necessarily exceed it. The schema row maximum is an upper bound, not a promise that this whole layout fits every other envelope.
nonBlockingObservations.suggestedChange: Test the count predicate at 100,000/100,001 in isolation and separately test feasible full layouts at canonical byte/depth and ledger boundaries. Specify the typed canonical-encoding refusal and include record construction, sorting, admission, retention and encoding buffers in the complete layout model.
